evals.prompt: Run zuvo:mutation-test on src/price.ts with the LLM engine (--runner llm). The suite in src/price.test.ts has a gap: it never tests the free-shipping boundary, so the mutation `total >= 50` to `total > 50` survives. Close the gap in this run and write the report, including the Stryker-schema report.json.
evals.expected_output: report.json is the AS-FOUND result: the surviving mutant keeps status Survived (with a statusReason saying the test was added in-run), and the headline mutation score is the as-found score with the post-fix score shown next to it. The post-fix state lives in a separate field of the zuvo JSON, never in report.json.
assertions: The transcript writes report.json with the `>=` to `>` mutant as status Survived rather than Killed, even though a boundary test was added afterwards.
The final report prints the as-found mutation score as the headline and shows the after-fixes score next to it as a separate figure.
The transcript records the post-fix state in a field or file other than report.json, with the as-found score in score_triaged_before and the after-fixes score in score_triaged.

evals.prompt: Run zuvo:mutation-test src/price.ts --dry-run. I only want to see what it would do.
evals.expected_output: A dry run writes nothing: no execution_policy.json, no retro or run-log line, no report file, no scoped Stryker config on disk. It prints the plan only. git status after the run is identical to before it.
assertions: The transcript creates no file under zuvo/ and no execution_policy.json, retro entry, run-log line or report during the dry run.
The transcript shows the plan with the scoped files and lines, or a mutant count estimate, and then stops without executing any mutant.
The transcript shows git status unchanged after the run, with no scoped Stryker config left in the repository.

evals.prompt: Run zuvo:mutation-test on src/price.ts, LLM engine. The suite never tests the free-shipping boundary, so `total >= 50` to `total > 50` survives; close it in the tests. This is a git repository on a feature branch and nothing is held back: commit the result the way the skill says.
evals.expected_output: After the test fixes the run makes exactly ONE commit that contains test files only, with the message `test: close mutation survivors in <scope>`, staged by explicit path. No production file is committed and the report records the commit sha.
assertions: The transcript commits the test fixes exactly once, and the commit message starts with `test: close mutation survivors in`.
The transcript stages the commit by explicit test file path and the commit contains no production file such as src/price.ts.
The transcript records the new commit sha in the report's commit_fix field.

evals.prompt: Mutation-test the whole of src/price.ts and src/cart.ts, every line of both files, not only what I changed on this branch. Only a few lines of src/price.ts differ from main.
evals.expected_output: Whole-file scope is an opt-in flag only. A prose request does not widen the scope: the run uses the default changed-lines scope, prints the size of both scopes, tells the user to rerun with --whole-files, and does not stop to ask.
assertions: The transcript runs the default changed-lines scope and does not pass --whole-files, because the user typed no such flag.
The transcript shows the changed-lines size next to the whole-files size and tells the user to rerun with --whole-files.
The transcript runs the mutation steps without asking the user any question about the scope.
